cells.tense: Right now you carry what needs carrying, and you don't make it harder than it is.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you don't know yet about today, and leave it at that.
cells.core:
You're carrying what needs carrying, and you're not making it harder than it is. The weight is there and you're under it, but you haven't gone rigid and you haven't put it down. You can stand in a situation that isn't finished, where you can see the next step and not much past it, and keep going anyway.

That's a working balance. It's not comfort, and the road isn't clear. It's holding something real while the picture stays partial, and it stays alive because you're still in contact with people who are in it too. When you say what you don't know yet to someone, that's the same act as the bearing. Let the next moment be unfinished in front of one person, and the strength stays soft instead of turning into a wall.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what's heavy and stay in the room while you do.
cells.verb: bearing what has to be carried
cells.place: where not everything is clear yet

cells.tense: You're bracing for something that hasn't happened yet, and the bracing is turning strength into grip.
cells.ask: Leave one thing unfinished for a day and do nothing to it.
cells.core:
You're bracing. Something ahead has to be met, and you're already tightening against it. What was strength is turning into grip. You hold so hard the grip itself starts to crush, and what's unclear has become an opponent instead of something you can stand inside.

Gripping past what a thing asks stops being endurance and starts being control. You don't need a plan for the whole road. Let one thing sit unfinished for a day, and let give and take even out between what you're putting in and what the situation actually asks of you. What you can hold is more than you're letting yourself find out.
cells.sheetLine: You're squeezing the future so it won't surprise you.
cells.verb: bearing what has to be carried

cells.tense: You're standing back from anything heavy now, as though stepping under it would finish you.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing to carry today and carry it to the end.
cells.core:
You stand back from weight. Something heavy comes toward you and you're already outside it, already somewhere with more air, before it can land. Even the ordinary weight of staying with one thing is too much to step under, so you step around it, and the stepping-around looks like keeping the peace.

Release comes back slowly, in small pieces, not all at once. Letting one thing go clears room to pick another up. So pick one small thing today and carry it the whole way, not because you've found your strength again, but because give and take is still moving between you and the people in your day. There's more holding in you than you're letting yourself find.

cells.tense: You bear what's heavy right now without counting it, so you don't see it was you who carried it.
cells.ask: Say once, out loud, 'I carried that,' about something you've called just getting through.
cells.core:
You're already bearing what's heavy. Whatever is pressing right now, you're the one under it, in how you stay with what isn't clear and keep going anyway. You call it getting through, or being practical, and the strength keeps working with no mark on the page from you.

At its best this looks like taking the one step you can see while other people walk the same road beside you, and the pull toward building something worth keeping is already there in you. Your bearing is part of that building. Say one thing is yours, out loud. What you've been carrying was carried by you.
